recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future cleanup of current R6 Specimen device example choice/canonical syntax should be handled under the later Specimen device-modeling issue family rather than reopening FHIR-39273.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive with Modification R5 OO issue asking to address Specimen characteristics deleted from R4 to R5. The final resolution required updating Specimen.processing.method to use descendants of SNOMED CT 9265001, fixing the broken specimen container example link on the General Specimen Example, and splitting any THO submission work into a separate ticket.
initial_application: The relevant application is visible in commit 560d03e820dcc52b95bb499232467d89e2ba66cd, merged by 5e5dc462ab3316d88b55b62fc9cda1a0abeb4a31. It moved specimen container Device examples under source/device, listed them in list-Device-examples.xml, updated Specimen examples away from old Specimen/specimen-device-container-* references, and changed source/specimen/valueset-specimen-processing-method.xml from a v2 include to a SNOMED CT descendent-of 9265001 include.
additional_context: Device, Specimen, and SpecimenDefinition are active current-build resources in source/fhir.ini. OO 2023-01-23 minutes confirm the value-set and General Specimen Example link motion. The THO split-out became FHIR-40646 and UP-408; FHIR-40646 was later Resolved - No Change because the core value set had already been updated and did not need to move to THO. Later R6 device-modeling work such as FHIR-39389 and FHIR-49751 affects current device representation but is separate from this R5 deletion cleanup tracker.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was needed because the current source already contains the SNOMED CT descendant filter, binds Specimen.processing.method to that value set, lists the target Device example, and no longer contains the old broken Specimen/specimen-device-container references.
